Connect.Title: Connect to a device
Connect.LanDevices: NexaDesk devices on the local network
Connect.LanSearching: Looking for NexaDesk devices on this network…
Connect.LanEmptyHelp: Not finding it? On the other computer, "Allow remote control" and "Show this Mac (PC) on the local network" must be on, and both computers must be on the same network. This Mac must also allow NexaDesk under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network.
Connect.LanEmptyHelp.Windows: Not finding it? On the other computer, "Allow remote control" and "Show this PC on the local network" must be on, and both computers must be on the same network. If Windows calls this network a public network, it may block discovery: make it a private network.
Connect.TailnetDevices: NexaDesk devices on your Tailscale network
Connect.TailscaleAdviceTitle: Not on the same local network? Use Tailscale
Connect.TailscaleAdvice: Install Tailscale on both devices and sign in to the same account to connect across networks. Tailscale does hole punching and falls back to a relay, so you need no server of your own. Once it is set up, the other device appears in the Tailscale device list.
Connect.NoRecent: You have not connected to any device yet.
Connect.Fingerprint: This Mac's fingerprint (the other person can compare it with the one they see when confirming the connection)
Connect.Fingerprint.Windows: This PC's fingerprint (the other person can compare it with the one they see when confirming the connection)
Connect.IntroWithId: Enter the address shown in the other person's window (a local network IP or Tailscale name) or their device ID, and the one-time code or their fixed password. With a device ID you can leave the code empty: you connect once they click Allow.
Connect.Intro: Enter the address shown in the other person's window (a local network IP or Tailscale name), and the one-time code or their fixed password.
Connect.AddressHint: Enter the other device's address: a local network IP or Tailscale name, optionally with a port (for example 192.168.1.20:47800)
Connect.IdNeedsServer: Device IDs work only after you set up a self-hosted signaling server (Advanced). To do without a server, install Tailscale on both devices and enter the other device's Tailscale name.
Connect.CodeHint: The one-time code is 8 letters or digits (2–7), for example ABCD-2345; a fixed password is at least 8 characters
Connect.NotPairedDetail: You have not paired with {0} yet. Enter the one-time code shown on their screen.
Connect.IdNeedsServerTitle: Device IDs need a signaling server
Connect.IdentityError: Could not load this Mac's identity: {0}
Connect.IdentityError.Windows: Could not load this PC's identity: {0}
Connect.RememberPasswordTip: Once it gets in, the fixed password is kept in the macOS Keychain: next time, one click in Recent signs in.
Connect.SavedPasswordInvalid: A fixed password is at least 8 characters and does not look like a one-time code.
Connect.AiAllowedHint: AI apps on this computer may connect to it through NexaDesk, which signs in with the saved password or by device ID. The person there is still asked and sees that it is an AI.
Connect.SavedPasswordFailed: Could not keep it in the Keychain: {0}
Connect.SavedPasswordStale: The saved password no longer works
Connect.SavedPasswordStaleDetail: {0}'s fixed password may have changed. The saved one was removed; type it again.
